topic: Antibiotic indication and review date documentation

audits.title: 1083 Assessment of Antibiotic Prescribing Compliance: Are We Adhering to NICE Guidelines for Recording Stop/Review Dates in Surgical Wards- A Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: NICE antimicrobial prescribing guidance: stop/review date recorded for antibiotics
audits.setting: Surgical ward, Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth
audits.intervention: Informal discussions and an email to junior doctors on findings and NICE guidance, plus posters in doctors' stations.
audits.other_findings: Causes included lack of awareness, patient transfers between teams and decisions documented on paper rather than electronic prescribing; a mandatory stop/review field in e-prescribing is proposed.
audits.citation: Noor M, Szentpali A, Anyanechi E, Ghosh A, Richardson J. 1083 Assessment of Antibiotic Prescribing Compliance: Are We Adhering to NICE Guidelines for Recording Stop/Review Dates in Surgical Wards- A Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.294.

audits.title: FP7.10 - An audit assessing the documentation of antibiotic indication and course length on an acute surgical unit
audits.standard: Documentation of antibiotic indication and course length on drug charts at prescription (recommended in numerous publications)
audits.setting: Acute surgical unit, district general hospital, East Sussex Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Indication documented in 54.0% and course length in 42.0%.

audits.intervention: Results presented to junior doctors and reminder cards attached to drug charts

cycle2.result: Indication documented in 74.0% and course length in 68.0%.

audits.other_findings: Co-amoxiclav and Tazocin were the most common agents in both cycles.
audits.citation: Carey C, Harshen R. FP7.10 - An audit assessing the documentation of antibiotic indication and course length on an acute surgical unit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.408.

audits.title: Sticking to minimum standards: implementing antibiotic stewardship in intensive care.
audits.standard: Minimum standards: documented start date, planned stop or review date and indication
audits.setting: 24-bed ICU, tertiary referral adult hospital, Melbourne
audits.intervention: Yellow medication record sticker, quarterly education sessions and ICU-specific empiric antimicrobial guidelines.
audits.other_findings: Documentation of minimum standards specifically addressed by the sticker improved.
audits.citation: Chaves NJ, Ingram RJ, MacIsaac CM, Buising KL. Sticking to minimum standards: implementing antibiotic stewardship in intensive care. Intern Med J. 2014;44(12a):1180-1187. doi:10.1111/imj.12539. PMID: 25070720.

audits.title: Antimicrobial stewardship: Improving antibiotic prescribing practice in a respiratory ward.

audits.title: Increasing the documentation of 48-hour antimicrobial reviews.
audits.setting: Two surgical wards, Darent Valley Hospital

cycle1.result: 18% of antimicrobial reviews completed at 48 hours

audits.intervention: Four PDSA cycles: trust-wide email, junior doctor teaching, sticker reminders in notes, presentation to consultants and ward posters
audits.other_findings: Most successful intervention was the consultant presentation with ward posters.
audits.citation: Sahota RS, Rajan KK, Comont JMS, Lee HH, Johnston N, James M, et al.. Increasing the documentation of 48-hour antimicrobial reviews. BMJ Open Qual. 2020;9(1):e000805. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2019-000805. PMID: 32034009.

audits.title: Development and implementation of a national antimicrobial stewardship surveillance system, with open access data sharing.
audits.standard: NHS AMR CQUIN: documentation of indication and 48-72 hour review
audits.setting: NHS hospital trusts in England (PHE AMS surveillance system)

cycle1.result: 33 trusts: on average 83% of patients had an indication documented and 71% had formal 48-72 h review documented.

audits.intervention: Refined national surveillance system linked to AMR CQUIN financial incentive

cycle2.result: About 92% of prescriptions had an indication documented and 87.5% had review within 72 h, rising by 7 and 10 percentage points between first and final quarters.

audits.other_findings: 88% of trusts submitted CQUIN data for at least one quarter; data published openly on PHE Fingertips.
audits.citation: Ashiru-Oredope D, Budd EL, Doble A, Cramp E, Hendrick A, Hopkins S. Development and implementation of a national antimicrobial stewardship surveillance system, with open access data sharing. J Hosp Infect. 2021;107:16-22. doi:10.1016/j.jhin.2020.10.015. PMID: 33122043.

audits.title: Potential to reduce antibiotic use in secondary care: Single-centre process audit of prescription duration using NICE guidance for common infections.
audits.standard: NICE guidance on antibiotic course length for common infections (CAP, HAP, pyelonephritis, cellulitis, IECOPD, cholangitis)
audits.setting: 750-bed acute secondary care hospital; single-centre process audit of medical inpatients

cycle1.result: 423 eligible; 307 (73%) notes reviewed; 173 met case definitions, 137 met short-course criteria. Potential antibiotic reductions (DDD): 32% in CAP, 20% in HAP, 14% in IECOPD, 11% in cellulitis, 10% in pyelonephritis.

audits.other_findings: Reductions estimated to cut total antibiotic use in medical specialties by 12.4%, equal to 3.6% of hospital total antibiotic use.
audits.citation: Powell N, Stephens J, Rule R, Phillips R, Morphew M, Garry E, et al.. Potential to reduce antibiotic use in secondary care: Single-centre process audit of prescription duration using NICE guidance for common infections. Clin Med (Lond). 2021;21(1):e39-e44. doi:10.7861/clinmed.2020-0141. PMID: 33479082.

audits.title: Compulsory Indications in Hospital Prescribing Software Tested with Antibacterial Prescriptions.
audits.standard: Documentation of indication on antibacterial prescriptions
audits.intervention: Indication field made compulsory in electronic prescribing for seven antibacterials
audits.other_findings: 'Other text' rose from 7.6% to 25.1%; an interactive report was developed for audit.
audits.citation: Pairman L, Chin P, Gardiner SJ, Doogue M. Compulsory Indications in Hospital Prescribing Software Tested with Antibacterial Prescriptions. AMIA Jt Summits Transl Sci Proc. 2024;2024:632-641. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-3199004/v1. PMID: 38827088.
